name: Bachelor of Arts and Entertainment Management
Bachelor of Music (Composition)
description:
The Composition stream at AIM runs on trimesters (AIM calls them study periods, three a year) rather than a conventional semester calendar, so students move through composition theory, arranging, orchestration, and soundtrack work at a different pace than a typical conservatorium degree.

Composition Module 1 opens the degree by setting out the compositional and production fundamentals the rest of the course builds on. From there, industry-focused units have students designing and producing a full musical work in collaboration with peers from AIM's performance and creative technology streams rather than composing in isolation. A mid-term proposal presentation and a formal delivery are both assessed. A dedicated self-management unit, unusual for a composition degree, addresses the practical realities of a freelance creative career: resilience, collaboration, and the business side most conservatoire training skips.

The degree closes with a Final Major Project in the last trimester: a portfolio of compositions, a recording, or a multimedia work, built under one-to-one supervision alongside masterclasses and guest lectures from working composers. Electives can be pulled from AIM's performance, production, management, media, and technology streams, letting a composition student pick up mixing skills or music business units rather than staying confined to a single track.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Composition Module 1; Music Theory and Aural Skills 1; Music History and Contextual Studies 1; 1 elective.
Study Period 2 — Composition Module 2; Arranging and Orchestration 1; Self-Management for Creative Practice; 1 elective.
Study Periods 3-4 — Composition Modules 3-4; Soundtrack and Media Composition; Collaborative Industry Project; electives.
Study Periods 5-6 — Advanced Composition; Portfolio Development; electives across performance, production, or business streams.
Final trimester — Final Major Project (composition portfolio, recording, or multimedia work); one-to-one supervision, masterclasses, guest lectures.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; portfolio/audition required

name: Bachelor of Music (Creative Technology)
description:
Creative Technology is AIM's production and audio engineering major, and it runs on a genuinely different clock to the rest of the institute's degrees: domestic students can complete it in 6 study periods (2 years full-time), while international students on visa-compliant course loads take 9 study periods (3 years): the same content, different pacing rules.

Foundational units get hands-on fast: DAW navigation and editing for both musical and non-musical audio, MIDI editing, signal processing (EQ, compression), virtual instruments, and fundamental mixing sit in the early units rather than being saved for later specialisation. From there the degree moves into recording theory, sound design, mixing, and mastering, treating studio technology as a creative instrument in its own right rather than purely a technical support skill for other musicians.

Entry requires an interview and a portfolio of two contrasting pieces, and because the degree sits alongside AIM's Performance, Composition, and Music Theatre majors on the same campus, Creative Technology students frequently end up mixing, recording, or scoring work for students in those other streams as part of their coursework rather than only working on their own material.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Audio Fundamentals and Acoustics; DAW Techniques 1; Music Theory for Producers.
Study Period 2 — Recording Theory 1; MIDI and Virtual Instruments; Signal Processing (EQ and Compression); 1 elective.
Study Periods 3-4 — Sound Design; Mixing Techniques; Collaborative Production Project (with Performance/Composition students); electives.
Study Periods 5-6 (domestic final study periods) — Mastering; Advanced Production Portfolio; Final Major Project.
Study Periods 7-9 (international students only) — extended major project and elective sequence over the additional year.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; audition/portfolio required

name: Bachelor of Music (Musicology)
description:
Musicology is AIM's non-performance major, built for students more interested in writing, researching, and critically engaging with music than performing it themselves, though a foundational level of practical musicianship is still expected. Coursework moves through music history and contextual studies, critical writing, and the theoretical and analytical skills used in scholarship, program notes, liner notes, and music journalism.

Because it sits inside the same trimester-based, industry-facing institution as AIM's performance majors, Musicology students study alongside performers, composers, and creative technology students rather than in an isolated academic track. Collaborative units draw them into critiquing and contextualising work being produced elsewhere in the building, a genuinely different experience to a musicology degree at a conventional university conservatorium.

Graduates go into music journalism, arts administration, artist management, music education, and further postgraduate research, with AIM's industry-facing culture giving Musicology graduates practical exposure to the music business that a purely academic musicology degree elsewhere often lacks.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Music History and Contextual Studies 1; Music Theory and Analysis 1; Introduction to Musicology; 1 elective.
Study Period 2 — Music History and Contextual Studies 2; Critical and Analytical Writing; 1 elective.
Study Periods 3-4 — Popular Music Studies; Music and Media; Research Methods; electives.
Study Periods 5-6 — Music Industry and Arts Management; Advanced Musicology Seminar; electives.
Final trimester — Musicology Capstone Project; portfolio of critical and analytical writing.

name: Bachelor of Music (Performance)
description:
Performance at AIM is built around weekly private lessons rather than group tuition as the spine of the degree. Performance Major units run as one-on-one instruction supported by a Performance Practice class of masterclasses, workshops, and seminars, so the individual teacher relationship, not a lecture theatre, is where most of the actual musical development happens.

Repertoire and technical demands escalate through the Performance Major sequence, but the degree also pushes students into collaboration outside their own instrument or voice, working with composition and Creative Technology students on new material rather than only performing established repertoire. Electives in entertainment management let performance students pick up the business side (booking, touring, artist management) without switching majors.

Entry requires a live audition or interview plus a portfolio of two live or recorded performances, a real filter reflecting AIM's position as an audition-based conservatoire rather than an open-entry university degree. AIM also runs a separate Classical strand of the Performance degree for students focused on that repertoire, distinct from the contemporary/commercial-leaning general Performance stream.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Performance Major 1 (weekly 1:1 lessons); Performance Practice 1; Music Theory and Aural Skills 1; 1 elective.
Study Period 2 — Performance Major 2; Performance Practice 2; Music History and Contextual Studies 1; 1 elective.
Study Periods 3-4 — Performance Major 3-4; Ensemble and Collaborative Performance (with Composition/Creative Technology students); electives.
Study Periods 5-6 — Performance Major 5-6; Advanced Performance Practice; entertainment management electives (optional).
Final trimester — Final Recital/Performance Project; portfolio and public performance assessment.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; audition required (two contrasting performance pieces)

name: Bachelor of Music Theatre
description:
Music Theatre at AIM trains across four disciplines at once: singing, dancing, acting, and creating, with one-on-one tuition in singing, dancing, and acting rather than folding those into shared group classes, an unusually resource-heavy structure for a music theatre degree.

Performance Skills units build the singing-actor specifically: students apply contemporary acting technique to vocal performance while deepening technical vocal work, rather than treating singing and acting as separate skills bolted together. Masterclasses, ensemble work, and live performance aren't extracurricular add-ons here; they're written directly into the coursework and assessed as part of it.

Delivery is face-to-face with some online components, typical for AIM's performance-based majors generally but worth noting for a discipline this practice-heavy: most of the actual training still happens in a studio or rehearsal room rather than online. Graduates head into professional music theatre, cabaret, and commercial theatre work, and the degree's dual training in singing and acting technique is built specifically for the audition demands of that industry.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Singing Technique 1 (1:1); Acting Technique 1 (1:1); Dance Technique 1; Performance Skills 1.
Study Period 2 — Singing Technique 2; Acting Technique 2; Dance Technique 2; Performance Skills 2; 1 elective.
Study Periods 3-4 — Singing-Actor Technique 3-4; Ensemble Music Theatre Workshop; Masterclass Series; electives.
Study Periods 5-6 — Advanced Performance Skills; Repertoire and Audition Preparation; electives.
Final trimester — Final Music Theatre Showcase (public performance); portfolio assessment.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; audition required (singing, acting, dance)

name: Diploma of Arts and Entertainment Management
Diploma of Music
description:
AIM's Diploma of Music is built as a genuine on-ramp rather than a watered-down bachelor's. Students cover Music History and Contextual Studies, Theoretical and Practical Application, and a Major Study in their chosen creative practice, and strong performers can transfer into the Bachelor of Music partway through based on progress and results rather than needing to reapply from scratch.

Entry asks for a resume of musical study or practical experience rather than the live audition and recorded portfolio required for AIM's bachelor's degrees, making the Diploma a lower-barrier entry point for students who haven't built an audition-ready portfolio yet but can demonstrate genuine musical background.

It functions as both a standalone qualification for students wanting a shorter, practice-focused credential and a pathway credential for those building toward a full Bachelor of Music, and the option to shift between the two based on results gives students a low-stakes way to test whether the full degree is the right fit.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Music History and Contextual Studies 1; Music Theory 1; Major Study 1 (practical).
Study Period 2 — Music History and Contextual Studies 2; Music Theory 2; Major Study 2 (practical); 1 elective.
Study Period 3 — Applied Musicianship; Major Study 3 (practical); 1 elective.
Study Period 4 — Performance and Portfolio Assessment; Major Study 4 (practical); pathway review for Bachelor of Music transfer.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; audition required

name: Graduate Diploma of Music
description:
AIM's Graduate Diploma of Music sits between the Master of Music and the undergraduate degrees: a shorter, more contained credential for graduates (in music or another field) wanting focused postgraduate-level training without committing to the full research-and-major-creative-project structure of the Master's.

Like the Master of Music, it runs across AIM's trimester calendar and draws on the same faculty of working composers, performers, and producers, but compresses the creative and research components into a single-year format rather than spreading them across a longer program. That's useful for career-changers or international graduates wanting a faster postgraduate qualification with an Australian credential attached.

It also functions as a bridge for students who complete a Graduate Certificate of Music and want to continue without committing immediately to the full Master's, or as a standalone finishing qualification for a specific creative or technical specialisation within music.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Advanced Creative Practice; Research Methods for Creative Practice; 1 elective.
Study Period 2 — Creative Project Development; Industry and Context subject; 1 elective.
Study Period 3 — Creative Project: Major Work; Presentation and Critique.
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in a related discipline, or equivalent audition/portfolio

name: Master of Arts and Entertainment Management
Master of Music
description:
AIM's Master of Music treats the degree less as coursework to complete and more as a vehicle for one significant, self-directed creative project: a festival, an album, a body of new compositions, a business plan for reaching new markets. Roughly half the program is built around delivering that project against milestones the student sets and refines with supervisors, with a further block of research subjects designed to sharpen and justify the creative direction rather than sit apart from it.

That project-first structure suits musicians already working professionally who want a credential and a structured runway to test an idea (a touring musician developing a new show, a producer building a label, a composer assembling a portfolio for film and screen work) more than someone coming straight from undergraduate study with no practice of their own yet.

AIM runs three intakes a year (trimesters, or "study periods" in AIM's own terminology) rather than the standard two-semester calendar, letting students start closer to when they're ready rather than waiting out a February or July cycle. Delivered from AIM's Surry Hills campus in Sydney, with faculty drawn from working composers, producers, and performers rather than purely academic staff.
curriculum:
Study Period 1 — Creative Project Proposal and Methodology; Research Methods for Creative Practice; 1 elective.
Study Period 2 — Creative Project Development 1; Research subject aligned to project; 1 elective.
Study Period 3 — Creative Project Development 2; Industry and Context subject.
Study Period 4 (final) — Creative Project: Major Work; Research subject aligned to project; presentation and critique.
admission_requirements: A recognised Bachelor's degree plus relevant professional experience in the music industry (or, without a bachelor's degree, admission may be offered on the basis of extensive professional experience). Applicants must also attend an interview or live audition and submit a portfolio of two contrasting pieces (digital or live) in their area of interest.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, with no band below 6.0 (AIM's published postgraduate/Master's English requirement).
